news.title: AI faculty search underway
news.summary_en: A faculty AI cluster hire is now underway across Danforth Campus schools. So far, more than 500 candidates have submitted applications.

news.title: US loses measles elimination status. What does that mean for Missouri?
news.summary_en: Jennifer Layden, MD, PhD, of WashU Bursky Public Health, explains how declining childhood vaccination rates threaten community protection and what families can do to reduce risks.

news.title: Epstein receives $11 million European Research Council Synergy Grant
news.summary_en: Lee Epstein, the Ethan A.H. Shepley Distinguished University Professor at WashU, and collaborators have received a grant from the European Research Council to examine how judges’ decisions affect democracy.

news.title: Provost West reappointed to role
news.summary_en: Mark D. West, executive vice chancellor for academic affairs and provost, has been reappointed to his role through June 2030.

news.title: Have we forgotten how dangerous measles can be?
news.summary_en: As measles resurges in the United States, infectious disease epidemiologist Catie Oldenburg explains what global vaccination successes can teach us about preventing its spread.

news.title: Brown School program works to move discoveries into real world
news.summary_en: A Brown School training program that has helped shape the field of implementation science for nearly two decades has received a new five-year federal grant, supporting its continued work to prepare researchers to bring scientific discoveries into everyday practice.

news.title: $43 million extends global study of inherited Alzheimer’s disease
news.summary_en: Funding from the NIH will help double enrollment in WashU Medicine’s Dominantly Inherited Alzheimer Network Observational Study (DIAN Obs) and explore why some people who inherit Alzheimer’s genes resist the disease.

news.title: Proposed SNAP cuts would mean more hungry children
news.summary_en: The Trump administration last week announced a proposed policy shift for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program that could strip benefits from millions. The change would devastate families already struggling due to updated eligibility rules, said Stephen Roll, at the WashU Brown School.

news.title: PAD presents ‘Top Girls’ Nov. 19-22
news.summary_en: Five exceptional women from history, folklore, literature and art gather for dinner. In “Top Girls,” British playwright Caryl Churchill explores gender, social expectation and definitions of success. WashU’s Performing Arts Department will present the celebrated drama Nov. 19-22.

news.title: Three WashU scholars were Rhodes finalists
news.summary_en: WashU senior Romen Der Manuelian and two recent alumni, Mason Shaver and Vincent Tsay, were finalists for the prestigious Rhodes Scholarship.
